description: DC Water publishes information about sanitary sewer overflows, spills of diluted untreated wastewater that can be caused by excessive rainfall, for the past five years, as a dashboard map broken down by year with a CSV download. The utility serves about 1,800 miles of sewer lines and asks the public to report suspected backups to its 24-hour Emergency Command Center, and it explains that its 2.6 billion dollar Clean Rivers Project adds combined sewer capacity and its storage tunnels may reduce some overflows. The dataset is updated monthly. Coverage: one city's sanitary sewer system, most recent five years, as event points. Access: free download; the licence is not stated, and a disclaimer limits use to public information about the programme and denies any accuracy guarantee. Caveats: the data are described as the best available at load time, so events may be revised, and field names were not inspected. It supports sewer capacity, overflow exposure and network flow analysis for a city, and relates to the EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass events data in the catalogue.
